summary: Nora can now hold a position in a conversation. After every turn — including the ones where she deliberately said nothing — a second model reads what just happened and revises one short paragraph about where the conversation stands, which she is then shown at the top of the next turn. Ships OFF; nothing about today's behaviour changes until an operator turns it on.
details: It is a SECOND model reading a FINISHED exchange, not her reflecting mid-turn. The argument is impartiality rather than cost: a model asked to judge its own reply while the reply is still to write is judging under social pressure. It is also the only way this can happen at all — the reply guard cancels the next model call once she has sent something, so nothing inside her own turn runs after the reply.

It reviews every completed turn, not only the ones that sent something. A turn where she chose to stay quiet produced just as much reasoning as one that replied, and a silence is the decision most likely to be wrong in a way nobody complains about. A debrief that only read successful replies would be measuring the path that already works.

The position is REVISED, never appended to. The fold is always shown the current position before it writes the next one, and that is the single non-negotiable of the design: the neighbouring tier shipped without it and accumulated two contradictory rows about the same thing, each unable to correct the other. There is a counter for it, so 'this fold read nothing' is a reading rather than an assumption.

It is capped at 1200 characters and the cap REFUSES rather than truncates. Over the limit, the model is handed back its own answer and asked to consolidate; if it still will not fit, nothing is written and the previous position stands. Silently dropping the oldest line is how a rolling position quietly becomes a summary of the last five minutes.

Nothing carrying a phone number, an account id or a coordinate is ever written into it. That is a new exposure rather than an old one: this paragraph is the only thing in her prompt that persists across turns instead of being rebuilt each time, so anything that got in would stay in by design.
limitations: Ships OFF ([standing] enabled = false), and it is the one optional capability whose work happens inside the live reply slot rather than in the background. The cost never lands on the person being reviewed — they already have their reply — it lands on the next person queued behind a busy conversation. Turning it on is a measured decision against nora_debrief_seconds (p95 <= 5s), not a default.

This is the position only. The design's other three outputs are not built: the per-turn verdict is the next phase, fact proposals are the one after that, and note proposals need the note store to grow the propose/supersede pair another workstream owns.
Because there is no per-turn verdict yet, nothing re-derives a position that has drifted. The raw material to rebuild one is retained, and the trigger for using it arrives with the verdict.
